name: Bug: Refine state-sync failure silently drifts nodes; dashboard counts diverge with no user-visible indicator

current_round.prompt:
From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: Bug: Refine state-sync failure silently drifts nodes; dashboard counts diverge with no user-visible indicator

Body:
Bug: Refine state-sync failure silently drifts nodes; dashboard counts diverge with no user-visible indicator

  Summary

  When a Refine daemon's git fetch origin fails (e.g. missing/expired credentials for the refine/state remote), state sync stops but the daemon keeps serving /dashboard, /nodes, and /work/goals
  from its stale local store. Nothing in the UI indicates the divergence. Users who compare per-node backlog cards against the "All" dashboard number see arithmetic that doesn't add up �X because
  each node's card is sourced from its own daemon while "All" is sourced from just one, and the daemons no longer agree on the underlying state.

  Environment

  - Refine version: 4.2.0 (per refine system status)
  - API contract: 2
  - Deployment: fleet of Linux dev boxes each running their own daemon on port 8082, sharing state via a refine/state branch on https://github.com/Insurity-Dev/ProSuite.git
  - Daemons observed: BO2LNXNEVO04 (QA) (node id default) and BO2LNXNEVO03 (Buddy) (node id bo2lnxnevo03-buddy)
  - Credential helper: store, backed by ~/.git-credentials

  Steps to reproduce

  1. Start two Refine daemons that sync via origin/refine/state over HTTPS.
  2. Remove or expire the github.com credential in ~/.git-credentials (in our case the file was rewritten and lost the GitHub entry on 2026-08-14 04:00 EDT).
  3. Continue creating/transitioning Goals on both daemons.
  4. Open the dashboard in a browser and compare:
    - The per-node card counts (from /nodes on each daemon)
    - The "All" total (from /dashboard?node=all on the daemon the browser is connected to)

  Expected behavior

  - Sync failures are surfaced prominently �X a banner on the dashboard, a needs_attention entry, or a health indicator on each node card.
  - If sync has failed for more than N minutes, the dashboard should refuse to display stale aggregate counts, or clearly label them "stale since <timestamp>".
  - The counts across nodes should reconcile (per-node backlogs sum to the "All" total from any daemon in the fleet).

  Actual behavior

  - Sync silently fails; last successful state-sync commit on refine/state at 2026-08-13 20:07 EDT. No banner, no dashboard warning, no needs_attention entry, no active_node_diagnostics �X the
  daemon just keeps serving stale counts.
  - Nothing in the daemon activity log (refine log query state, refine log query sync, or the state/sync/push/fetch categories) mentions the ongoing failure. The failure is only visible if a user
  (a) manually clicks Sync or (b) hits POST /project/sync directly, at which point the returned operation object contains:
  {
    "state": "Failed",
    "error": {
      "code": "project_sync_failed",
      "message": "git fetch --prune origin failed: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled"
    }
  }
  - Because each node's card is sourced from its own daemon (each daemon reports its own view authoritatively), and "All" comes from just one daemon's local total, the numbers stop reconciling.
  Concrete snapshot from 2026-08-15 ~08:47 UTC:

  | Query                                                      | QA daemon | Buddy daemon |
  |------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------|
  | /nodes �� counts["default"].backlog (QA node)               | 95        | 0            |
  | /nodes �� counts["bo2lnxnevo03-buddy"].backlog (Buddy node) | 73        | 109          |
  | /nodes �� counts["bo2lnx-kxion"].backlog                    | (absent)  | 6            |
  | /dashboard?node=all �� counts.backlog                       | 168       | 115          |

  - UI observation: QA card = 95, Buddy card = 109, "All" = 115. 95 + 109 �� 115 because the 95 QA backlog goals only exist on QA's daemon (Buddy sees 0), and the 6 kxion backlog goals only exist
  on Buddy's daemon.

  Impact

  - Users lose trust in the counts. In our case a user (Buddy) noticed the arithmetic mismatch and had to file a bug to find out sync was broken. Without that noticing, both daemons would have
  continued drifting indefinitely.
  - Goals created on one node never reach other nodes' workflow runners. Anyone who queues work on a node other than where the goal was authored will silently sit idle.
  - Approvals / status transitions taken on one node are invisible to another �X an approver could re-approve work that was already approved elsewhere, or a "done" goal could be re-implemented on
  the other node.
  - Reporting numbers (dashboard, assignee_stats, "counts" in support bundles) become per-daemon opinions, not facts.

  Root cause (from code inspection)

  - src/tools/host/git_sync/service.rs:sync_locked runs git fetch against origin before reconciling the local store with the remote refine/state branch (line 113). If fetch fails, the function
  returns an error and no reconciliation happens. There is no fallback path that surfaces the persistent-failure state to the UI.
  - The dashboard summary in src/tools/product/project_projection/query.rs:dashboard_summary (line 35) computes all_node_counts from self.goals.values() �X i.e., whatever this daemon has in its
  local projection. It has no notion of "the fleet's authoritative total," so a lagged daemon happily reports its stale view as all_node_counts.
  - handle_dashboard in src/surfaces/web_server/project_routes/dashboard.rs populates needs_attention only from failed_count (line 87�V92) and runner_reachable/workflow_paused �X nothing about sync
  freshness.
  - The audit trail at .git/refine-audit.jsonl records only git_path / worktree / worktree_remove actions; there is no sync_failed or fetch_failed action being emitted for the automatic git-sync
  worker path.

  Suggested fix

  Any of these would independently resolve the "silent divergence" class of bug �X ideally all three:
  1. Surface sync freshness on the dashboard. Add a "state-sync last succeeded at <timestamp>" field to /dashboard and populate needs_attention with a warning if the last successful sync is older
  than some threshold (e.g., state_sync_debounce_seconds * 10, or a settable stale-sync threshold).
  2. Log automatic sync failures to the activity log. The daemon's git-sync worker (refine system runner-worker --kind git-sync) currently only records failures if a user manually triggers POST
  /project/sync. Every failed automatic attempt should record a sync_failed activity entry with the underlying git error, visible via refine log query.
  3. Fail loudly per-node in /nodes. Each node record should include a health field indicating whether that daemon's own sync is healthy, and the UI should render an error state on the card if
  not.

  Optional bonus: detect when the count arithmetic can't be reconciled (sum(per-node backlog) != all_node_counts.backlog) and surface that as a diagnostic �X that's a definitive tell that this
  daemon has partial knowledge.

  Workaround

  On each affected daemon host:
  # Restore GitHub credential:
  echo "https://<user>:<PAT>@github.com" >> ~/.git-credentials
  chmod 600 ~/.git-credentials

  # Trigger a resync:
  curl -sX POST http://localhost:8082/project/sync
  Confirm success by checking that the returned operation reaches state: "Succeeded" and that refine/state HEAD advances in the state worktree at <repo>/.git/refine-state-worktree.

  Evidence attachments (for the ticket body)

  - Manual sync failure payload (both daemons, identical): {"code":"project_sync_failed","message":"git fetch --prune origin failed: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com':
  terminal prompts disabled"}
  - Last successful state-sync commit on QA: 91738db751 Sync Refine state: 1 goal at 2026-08-13 20:07:50 -0400
  - ~/.git-credentials mtime on QA: 2026-08-14 04:00, contents scope: dev.azure.com only
  - Daemon uptime since restart on QA: active (running) since Fri 2026-08-14 08:49:34 EDT �X has never successfully synced during this run

findings.description: Appending a shared activity entry for every automatic failure is unsafe: the worker retries failed remote fetches every two seconds, logs/activity.jsonl is synchronized durable state, and concurrent outage entries from multiple nodes become a conflicting non-Goal path that can prevent convergence after credentials are restored.
findings.recommendation: Record redacted failure episodes on transitions with bounded repeats and a recovery event, using runtime-local activity projected into log queries or a tested stable-ID append-only merge before placing the evidence in synchronized activity.

findings.description: The plan adds runtime-local health and read contracts but no event or timer path for health transitions; current dashboard and node views refresh from SSE, so an open page can miss a failure, stale-threshold crossing, or recovery until an unrelated event or reload.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit state-sync-health SSE/revision contract and refresh affected surfaces on failure, staleness, and recovery transitions, including the time-based stale boundary.

result.summary: Revise failure evidence ownership and live health notification before implementation.

checklist.description: Add a validated node setting for the state-sync stale threshold whose default exceeds the normal remote-fetch cadence and make the Git-sync schedule expose that threshold.

Create a cohesive runtime-local state-sync health service that atomically binds health to the active target and node, records attempts, last successful reconciliation, failure episodes, redacted errors, and a monotonic revision, and treats lock deferrals, intentional pauses, and an unconfigured remote as neutral rather than failed.

Route automatic and manual Git-sync outcomes through the health service, clear an outage only after successful reconciliation, and project one node-local failure-transition entry, bounded reminders, and one recovery entry into existing activity and log queries without synchronizing those records on refine/state.

Add a typed state-sync-health SSE contract whose time-aware fingerprint changes on failure, stale-threshold crossing, and recovery, and have browser SSE and reconnect reconciliation refresh dashboard, node, and log surfaces from their authoritative read endpoints.

Extend the dashboard contract and browser view with last-attempt, last-success, failure, and stale-since metadata, add prominent needs_attention state for failed or stale sync, and label locally projected all-node counts non-authoritative while health is degraded.

Extend the nodes contract and browser node presentation so the serving daemon reports sync health for its active node and reports other nodes as unknown unless local evidence exists, without changing existing fleet bootstrap health semantics.

Update the affected fleet, activity-and-evidence, dashboard, settings, and API intent contracts to document node-local sync health, transition-based outage evidence, SSE freshness updates, and the non-authoritative boundary for stale aggregates.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: Replace synchronized per-retry activity writes with node-local failure episodes, bounded reminders, and recovery records that are merged into normal log queries, preventing two-second retry storms and cross-node state conflicts.
Include derived sync health in a typed SSE fingerprint that evaluates the wall-clock stale boundary and refreshes affected surfaces on failure, staleness, recovery, initial connection, and reconnect.

result.summary: Refine will maintain node-local state-sync health and outage evidence, expose freshness through daemon read contracts and SSE, and visibly downgrade stale dashboard aggregates so credential or fetch failures cannot leave fleet counts looking authoritative while nodes drift.

checklist.evidence: Added validated state_sync_stale_threshold_seconds setting (1..86400), default 900 seconds versus the normal 300-second remote-fetch cadence, exposed through GitSyncSchedule and runtime Settings UI.

Added cohesive FileStateSyncHealthService with locked atomic replacement, canonical target/node binding, attempts, successes, failure episodes, redacted errors, neutral deferred/unconfigured outcomes, pause-aware derived health, and revision continuity across rebinds.

Automatic git-sync and manual project-sync now record shared health outcomes; activity emits one local-only state_sync failure transition, reminders no more often than every 30 minutes, and one recovery transition, while logs remain excluded from refine/state.

Added typed state_sync_health SSE state and semantic fingerprint over status, success, failure, stale boundary, and error; browser handlers reconcile Dashboard, Logs, and Node/Settings surfaces and existing onopen logic handles initial/reconnect reads.

Dashboard API and UI expose status, attempt/success/failure/stale timestamps, redacted error, stale threshold, prominent failed/stale needs_attention, and explicit local-projection/non-authoritative aggregate labeling while degraded.

Nodes API and Settings Nodes table expose state_sync_health for the serving daemon's active node and explicit unknown/node_local_evidence_unavailable for other nodes without modifying existing fleet bootstrap health.
Updated fleet, activity/evidence, Dashboard, Settings, and API intent pages with node-local health, outage evidence, SSE freshness, and aggregate authority contracts.

checklist.description: Add a cohesive state-sync health service that atomically tracks the current target, last attempt, last success, latest sanitized failure, and configured stale threshold without treating lock deferrals, intentional pauses, or an unconfigured remote as sync failures.

Route automatic and manual Git-sync outcomes through the health service, append a searchable sync_failed activity entry for every failed automatic attempt with the underlying Git error, and clear the active failure only after a real successful reconciliation.
Add a node-runtime setting for the stale-sync threshold with a safe default longer than the normal remote-fetch cadence and expose it through the existing Settings contract.

Extend the dashboard response with sync health and stale-since metadata, add a prominent needs_attention banner for failed or stale sync, and label aggregate counts as stale rather than presenting the daemon's local projection as fleet-authoritative.

result.summary: Refine will persist each daemon's state-sync freshness and failures as runtime-local health, record automatic sync failures in the shared activity trail, and expose that health through dashboard and node contracts so locally computed fleet counts are clearly marked non-authoritative when synchronization is stale instead of silently appearing consistent.
